name: item_move_whole_set
description: Frozen reference behaviour: an item-mode translate moves the WHOLE selected set, not just the distinguished item. Three items are selected and given a single translate of -1.2 on Y; all three land -1.2 lower and none of them moves on X. Companion to item_acen_primary_of_three: the shared centre follows the primary alone, but the motion applies to every selected item — the two are deliberately NOT the same set.
source: Frozen reference capture (headless, scripted): a numeric translate attribute followed by an apply, read back as per-item positions. Two different transform configurations produced identical results.

provenance.harness: private headless capture harness (scripts + per-case result JSON live in the private tree)
provenance.notes: Driven as a numeric attribute + apply rather than a viewport drag, so the amount is exact rather than pixel-derived. The X column is asserted UNCHANGED as well as the Y column moved: an implementation that moved the set along the wrong axis, or that rebased every item onto the shared centre, would disturb X.
provenance.post_capture_rig_change: The scene ORDER of the three items was permuted (0, 6, 2 -> 0, 2, 6) and the ADD order with it, to close a defect in the companion fixture item_acen_primary_of_three: there the distinguished item was also the last item created, so an implementation reading the last layer passed by construction. The permutation reorders the rows of `expected.before` / `expected.after` / `rejected[].after` and changes nothing else — the same three items get the same delta, and the frozen law ('every selected item translates by the same world delta') is order-blind. Recorded rather than silently applied: this is a rig edit made AFTER the capture.

rig.comment: Shared for real with item_acen_primary_of_three — one builder (tests/item_rig_helpers.d) and this identical `rig` block, which both tests check against the other fixture's copy. The two fixtures pin the centre and the moving set on ONE state, so the rigs must not drift apart.

expected.law: every selected item translates by the same world delta; the distinguished item is not privileged in the motion

rejected.candidate: the set collapses onto the shared centre

classification.detail: vibe3d binds the item transform to the whole selected item set and translates each about the shared frozen centre; the measured after-positions are identical to the reference's, including the untouched X column. This fixture is a LIVE test that must pass.
